title: National Service – Balancing Operational Readiness, Safety and the Will to Fight
what_it_is: National Service – Balancing Operational Readiness, Safety and the Will to Fight

sections.label: MINDEF zero training deaths goal
sections.summary: MINDEF's message of making zero training deaths the norm is unrealistic and wishful given inherent military training risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, training safety must always be of the utmost importance for MINDEF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, MINDEF's recent message to make, and I quote, "zero training deaths the norm" is not only unrealistic but also wishful, considering the inherent risks in training a military force that must be ready to defend the country at a moment's notice or whenever called upon to do so.

sections.label: Zero-accident mindset after Pang's death
sections.summary: MINDEF's narrative shifted to a zero-accident mindset, but zero accidents cannot be achieved even in strict industries like aviation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the aftermath of CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang's passing, MINDEF's narrative has shifted somewhat to, I quote, "a zero-accident mindset".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NSmen and those who are familiar with the SAF understand what MINDEF wants to achieve when it speaks of striving for zero fatalities – that MINDEF takes safety seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the word that the public focuses on is "zero", and the end state of zero-accidents or fatalities is a goal that cannot be achieved even in industries with notoriously strict safety standards and compliance requirements like aviation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in October 2015, maintenance engineers did not follow established procedures to insert landing gear pins before troubleshooting a landing gear fault causing a Singapore Airlines A330's nose-wheel to collapse at the boarding gate, resulting in multi-million dollars' worth of damage.

sections.label: SAF safety review perception
sections.summary: The speaker supports the SAF safety review but says it must not create a perception that the SAF has gone soft.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As much as I support the safety review currently being undertaken by the SAF, it must not lead to a public perception that the SAF has gone soft.

sections.label: Discussions damaging institution of NS
sections.summary: Discussions after CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang's passing could damage the institution of NS unless MINDEF addresses broader misgivings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a result of the recent incidents, some of the discussions in the aftermath of CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang's passing have the potential of damaging the institution of NS unless MINDEF steps in to decisively address broader misgivings that are simmering in the minds of some Singaporeans.

sections.label: Proposed MINDEF defence White Paper
sections.summary: The speaker proposed MINDEF publish a detailed defence White Paper outlining SAF strategic imperatives after a Committee of Supply cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some years ago, on the back of a Committee of Supply cut, I proposed that MINDEF publish a detailed defence White Paper outlining the strategic imperatives of SAF.

sections.label: Training deaths shaking NS support
sections.summary: Despite earlier surveys showing public support for NS, the recent spate of training deaths shows the status quo can be shaken quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In spite of earlier surveys highlighted in this House about the public's support for NS, the recent spate of training deaths reminds us how the status quo can be shaken very quickly.

sections.label: Stretching officer retirement ages
sections.summary: MINDEF should consider stretching the retirement ages of the officer and WOSE corps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One approach MINDEF should consider is stretching the retirement ages of the officer and WOSE corps.

sections.label: Retaining officers and WOSEs
sections.summary: SAF should emphasise retaining officers and WOSEs after retirement, and the 18-year-old NS cohort will shrink by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, SAF should also pay particular emphasis on retaining officers and WOSEs after they retire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A second area of consideration for MINDEF deals with the point that in the run-up to 2030, the cohort of 18-year-olds enlisted for NS is going to get smaller.

sections.label: Review of Government Proceedings Act
sections.summary: A qualitative way to facilitate this must include reviewing the Government's position on section 14 of the Government Proceedings Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From a legislative perspective, a qualitative way to facilitate this must include a review of the Government's position on section 14 of the Government Proceedings Act.

sections.label: Carve-out for safety disregard
sections.summary: The Government could inject greater accountability by creating a carve-out for willful disregard of safety factors under section 14.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To drive home the centrality of safety for the SAF's peacetime mission, there is room for the Government to inject greater accountability into its protocols and processes by creating a specific carve-out for willful disregard of safety factors under section 14 of the Government Proceedings Act.

sections.label: Exception for reckless commanders
sections.summary: A training safety exception to section 14 would apply only if a commander behaves recklessly, maliciously or with willful disregard for safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address such legitimate concerns, a possible exception to section 14 on the grounds of training safety would only apply if a commander behaves recklessly, maliciously or displays a willful disregard for safety considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, if a commander had deliberately chosen to cancel a safety briefing, disregarded training safety regulations, had not catered for sufficient rest before or between training and missions without adequate reason or risk mitigation approved beforehand by a more senior commander, then the blanket immunity provided under section 14 should not apply.

sections.label: Fighter losses 1970 to 1990
sections.summary: From 1970 to 1990 Singapore lost almost as many fighters as its entire F-16 fleet today, while the RSAF lost two F-16s since about 1996/1997.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For the first 20 years from 1970 to 1990, we lost in terms of fighter numbers, almost the same number as our entire F-16 fleet today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For comparison, the RSAF has operated the F-16 C/Ds for more than 20 years now from about 1996/1997, and we have lost two.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And the last loss occurred more than 10 years ago." That is a stark difference.

sections.label: Zero fatality training goal
sections.summary: The zero fatality goal makes commanders and soldiers careful, with safety lapses not tolerated, so soldiers stay alive to fight for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Can anyone guarantee that there will be zero fatalities for the rest of our future?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But that zero fatality goal sears into the consciousness of every commander and every soldier that, to get there, you better be careful about what you are doing, that safety lapses will not be tolerated, that it will be safety first, because, at the end of the day, I want to train you and want you to be alive to be able to fight when Singapore needs you.
